recommendation: Keep this audit as-is. Do not change Resource.id under this issue, and do not edit tools/history release cache files solely to rewrite historical R4B/R5 metadata; any historical technical-correction publication should be handled through the publication/generator path.
issue_request: FHIR-36036 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-I technical correction for R4B/R5 reporting that generated backbone element ids such as Patient.contact.id carried fhir-type id when they should use the string flavor inherited from Element.id.
initial_application: No direct FHIR source commit for FHIR-36036 was found. The application path is HL7/kindling#69, merged 2022-04-07, whose body says it corrected FHIRtype extension values for FHIR-36036 and whose first commit is titled with the Jira URL.
additional_context: FHIR-25274 documents the FHIRPath System.String plus structuredefinition-fhir-type pattern, and FHIR-25262 keeps Resource.id distinct as fhir-type id. FHIR-I minutes record FHIR-36036 as a technical correction/tooling issue. Later FHIR-38684 and FHIR-41183 audits are already on the combined branch and confirm the current-output correction for adjacent Element.id and ElementDefinition.id cases. Historical R4B/R5 base BackboneElement artifacts can still show id, but current build output is corrected.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The active source has Element.@id as type string, BackboneElement derives from Element without a separate id row, and current build.fhir.org profiles for Patient.contact.id, BackboneElement.id, Element.id, and ElementDefinition.id all emit fhir-type string.
